newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Fischer says sold shares recently.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Fischer says sold shares recently.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Wednesday he had sold his shares in BHP in the last few days.
"I took the additional steps of liquidating a portfolio, including the sale of BHP shares," Fischer told parliament.
"And that sale of the BHP shares has been in the last few days," he said.
An Australian Financial Review newspaper report on Wednesday said Fischer had sold shares in major mining and exporting companies over the last few months with some as recently as last week.
The newspaper report said Fischer's holdings had included shares in Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Clyde Industries Ltd, WMC Ltd, Qantas Airways Ltd and TNT Ltd.
Fischer's ministerial responsibility includes promoting Australian trade.

Fischer denied in a radio interview that he had breached Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial guidelines, under which government members are required to dispose of investments which might conflict with their portfolio area.
Prime Minister John Howard said earlier on Wednesday it was absurd to suggest Fischer had breached ministerial guidelines.
Howard has said the guidelines may be too strict and should be reviewed.
The share row over conflict of interests has already claimed two government members.
Jim Short quit as assistant treasurer on Sunday and Brian Gibson resigned from his position as parliamentary secretary to the treasurer on Tuesday.
Both chose to resign after their own staff found evidence of a conflict of interest in particular ministerial decisions.
